# 2. Lists and procedures

<!-- Generated by tools/generate-docs.lisp from docs/manual/chapters.lisp,
     docs/manual/introduction.md and the examples: do not edit by hand. -->

Lists are made of pairs, and procedures are values that keep the variables
they were made with.

## Building and taking apart lists

`examples/lists.lisp`:

```scheme
(define nums '(1 2 3 4 5))

(define (show label value)
  (display label)
  (display ": ")
  (display value)
  (newline))

(show "squares" (map (lambda (x) (* x x)) nums))
(show "appended" (append nums '(6 7)))
(show "reversed" (reverse nums))

; keep only the elements that satisfy keep?: the built-in filter does this; here
; is how such a procedure is written
(define (keep-if keep? lst)
  (if (null? lst)
      '()
      (if (keep? (car lst))
          (cons (car lst) (keep-if keep? (cdr lst)))
          (keep-if keep? (cdr lst)))))

(show "evens" (keep-if (lambda (n) (= (modulo n 2) 0)) nums))

(define (sum lst)
  (if (null? lst)
      0
      (+ (car lst) (sum (cdr lst)))))

(show "sum" (sum nums))
(show "a dotted pair" (cons 'a 'b))
```

Its output:

```text
squares: (1 4 9 16 25)
appended: (1 2 3 4 5 6 7)
reversed: (5 4 3 2 1)
evens: (2 4)
sum: 15
a dotted pair: (a . b)
```

## Assigning to a place: set! of a list's element, a vector's slot, a table's entry

set! takes a variable, or a call that names a place: (set! (car x) v) sets
the first element of x. This is SRFI 17's generalized set!: it calls
((setter car) x v), and car's setter is set-car!. The built-in getters
(car, cdr, vector-ref, string-ref, hash-table-ref, hash-table-ref/default)
have setters, and a program gives its own procedure one with
(set! (setter f) g).

`examples/places.lisp`:

```scheme
(define x (list 'a 'b 'c))
(set! (car x) 'n)
(display x) (newline)

(define board (vector '- '- '-))
(set! (vector-ref board 1) 'x)
(display board) (newline)

; a counter: hash-table-ref/default's setter ignores the default
(define seen (make-hash-table))
(for-each (lambda (word)
            (set! (hash-table-ref/default seen word 0)
                  (+ 1 (hash-table-ref/default seen word 0))))
          '("to" "be" "or" "not" "to" "be"))
(display (list (hash-table-ref seen "to") (hash-table-ref seen "or"))) (newline)

; a getter of our own, with its setter
(define (middle triple) (car (cdr triple)))
(set! (setter middle) (lambda (triple value) (set-car! (cdr triple) value)))
(define t3 (list 1 2 3))
(set! (middle t3) 'two)
(display t3) (newline)
```

Its output:

```text
(n b c)
#(- x -)
(2 1)
(1 two 3)
```

## Each counter keeps its own private state

`examples/closures.lisp`:

```scheme
(define (make-counter)
  (let ((count 0))
    (lambda ()
      (set! count (+ count 1))
      count)))

(define a (make-counter))
(define b (make-counter))

(a)
(a)
(a)
(b)

(display "a has counted to ")
(display (a))
(display ", b to ")
(display (b))
(newline)

; procedures remember the text they were compiled from
(display (procedure-source make-counter))
(newline)
```

Its output:

```text
a has counted to 4, b to 2
(define (make-counter)
  (let ((count 0))
    (lambda ()
      (set! count (+ count 1))
      count)))
```
